messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: KV-cache memory surge on hosted-runtime-prod (pool a-3). Multiple OOMs observed across replica set, elevated error rate starting 02:07 UTC. Please acknowledge.

marta: acked. seeing 5xx spike in the runtime dashboard, traces show large context windows triggering heavy prefetch.

alex: on it. initial hypothesis: continuous-batching + aggressive prefetch -> kv shards growing without eviction.

priya: customer-facing impact: 4 customers with high-usage workloads reported 504/timeouts; internal metrics show request latency jumping from 120ms -> 2-6s for affected calls.

ben: logs from node-17 (extract):
```
[2026-03-15T02:07:12Z] runtime: kvcache shard 12 size=65.1GB limit=64GB
[2026-03-15T02:07:12Z] runtime: OutOfMemoryError: region kv-cache alloc failed
[2026-03-15T02:07:12Z] runtime: continuous-batcher drained 0/0 pending (backpressure)
```

marta: ok mitigation plan: 1) disable prefix prefetch on hosted runtime 2) cap continuous-batcher window to 3 tokens per request (temporary) 3) force aggressive eviction on KV cache (LRU -> TTL short) 4) canary config push to pool a-3 then scale out if stable. anyone object?

alex: +1. also suggest applying a short-lived per-request max_context_tokens override (60k) for hosted tier to prevent single-request blowups.

ben: prepping hotfix patch now. patch is small config toggle in runtime-configs: `kv.prefetch.enabled=false`, `batcher.max_window=3`, `kv.eviction.policy=aggressive`

ben: pushing hotfix to canary subset (node-17, node-21) -> deploy-bot: starting deploy.

deploy-bot: deploy 1925487650-hotfix-config -> canary nodes [node-17,node-21] STARTED

marta: notifying support & PGs: posting incident banner on status page and flagging customers who saw 504s.

priya: status update for customers: short note drafted, will send once canary stabilization confirmed.

ben: canary logs: nodes show immediate drop in KV growth. no new OOMs in 90s, p50 latency dropping back toward baseline.

deploy-bot: canary deploy SUCCEEDED -> promoting to remainder of pool a-3 (rolling).

carol: taking handoff in 15m. summary for next oncall: root cause likely prefetch + continuous-batching interaction exposing a KV cache eviction gap; hotfix disables prefetch + tightens batch window; monitor for regression and potential QoS impact (more compute per token). checklist: 1) confirm all nodes at new config 2) watch OOMs and eviction churn 3) re-enable prefetch only after adding per-request prefetch limits and stronger eviction/TTL 4) coordinate with platform to roll a permanent guard (token caps per request) 5) follow-up postmortem.

marta: good handoff. tagging infra and runtime teams for follow-up: @alex @ben @carol.

alex: note for postmortem: add telemetry to track per-shard KV growth vs incoming sequence-length distribution; we missed warning signs.

priya: customer comms sent to impacted customers (short incident notice + mitigation actions). asked CS to escalate severe customers.

carol: taking lead. will run a 30m vigilance window then hand back if stable. leaving this thread open for updates. :white_check_mark:
